newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee seen building base, called higher.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee seen building base, called higher.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
LIFFE coffee futures were called to open $70 up on numbers on Wednesday after a strong New York performance overnight but traders said it could stop at $15-$20.
Technically, analysts said the market was likely to continue its base-building following the recent sharp downward move, before attempting another rally.
Susan Rigg, an analyst at Chart Analysis, said coffee continued to hold above boundaries of support.
But the technical picture remained weak.
On the upside, the $2,000 level basis September was seen more as a psychological barrier than anything else.
The last time the contract held above $2,000 was on June 10 and well below the twin peaks of $2,700 in late May.
Rigg said a break beneath $1,700 support would be significant but there was a lot of support beneath that.
She said the market might have a chance of another rally. But after the big down move recently, it was unlikely to get to $2,000 in a hurry.
"It may have some support-building work to do," she said.
New York arabica futures ended Tuesday higher, bolstered by speculative buying amid an USDA attache report for the 1997/98 Brazil crop.

The attache report, dated May 9, put Brazil's 1997/98 harvest at 24 million 60-kg bags, down sharply from the USDA's official Brazil estimate of 28 million bags published in its 1997/98 world coffee production report in June.
